nonLabourLines.description: Legacy data migration tooling & Oracle export licenses

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; hour estimates are derived from story points using a rough Fibonacci-to-hours heuristic (1 point ≈ 6-7 effective hours) and typical task composition, not measured velocity.
1 story point ≈ 6.5 effective hours across the team, split by task type (e.g., migration and RBAC skew heavily backend/QA, design system skews frontend).

Backend Developer is staffed at 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/month capacity); the 620 allocated hours implies roughly 2.6 months of full backend team capacity dedicated to this backlog, which is reasonable given the backlog is backend-heavy (auth, RBAC, payments, migration).

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/month); the 110 hours allocated for CI/staging setup and Stripe webhook infra consumes nearly 2 months of that capacity, so DevOps is a thin resource and could become a bottleneck if other infra needs arise.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~96 hrs/month) is allocated 220 hours (~2.3 months) concentrated on the higher-risk items: auth, RBAC, payments, and migration validation; lower-priority items get lighter QA pass.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as the highest-uncertainty item, driving most of the pessimistic-scenario spread, due to unknowns in legacy Oracle schema quality and data volume (400k records / 2M invoice lines).
Payment provider integration (PW-7) includes a fixed non-labour cost for PCI-related compliance review/tooling in addition to engineering hours.
Non-labour costs assume a 3-month project timeline for staging/CI infrastructure and one-off licensing/tooling costs for the Oracle migration.
Design system (PW-2) and Invoice list/detail (PW-6), both Medium priority, are the first candidates for descoping or deferral if budget needs to shrink.
Estimate assumes no major scope changes to requirements once work begins and no significant legacy schema surprises beyond normal migration risk.
input.reasoning: Hours were allocated per backlog item by translating story points into effective hours (~6.5 hrs/point) and then splitting across roles based on the nature of each task: CI/staging (PW-1) is DevOps + some Backend; the design system (PW-2) is almost entirely Frontend with light QA; registration/login (PW-3) and RBAC (PW-4) are Backend-heavy with Frontend and QA support; the dashboard (PW-5) and invoice views (PW-6) are Frontend-led with Backend API work and QA; payment integration (PW-7) is Backend-heavy with QA and a DevOps slice for webhook infra, plus a compliance non-labour cost; legacy data migration (PW-8) is the largest single driver of Backend and QA hours given its size (21 points) and criticality, plus dedicated migration tooling cost. Role hour totals were checked against each role's FTE capacity to flag thin staffing (DevOps and QA are the tightest). The Most Likely scenario equals the sum of all line items; Optimistic assumes ~14% efficiency gains (less rework, no migration surprises) and Pessimistic assumes ~20% overrun (migration complexity, payment reconciliation edge cases, RBAC scope creep), consistent with the higher uncertainty on Urgent/High items. Priority breakdown allocates each backlog item's full labour+non-labour cost to its priority tier: Urgent (PW-3, PW-7), High (PW-1, PW-4, PW-5, PW-8), Medium (PW-2, PW-6).

reductions.description: Descope or defer the Design System component library (PW-2) to a later phase, reusing basic Angular Material components instead of a fully custom theming system for launch.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~100 and QA hours by ~10; delays a reusable component library but does not block core customer-facing flows for initial launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on lower-risk Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) by relying more on automated regression tests instead of full manual QA passes.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA hours; increases regression risk on invoice list/detail and design system components, mitigated by automated test coverage.

reductions.description: Phase the Legacy Data Migration (PW-8): migrate the most recent 12 months of invoice lines first and backfill the remainder post-launch instead of migrating all 2M lines upfront.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend and QA migration hours by roughly 120 combined and shrinks the migration tooling/license non-labour cost; introduces a follow-up project phase to complete the historical backfill.

reductions.description: Defer the 3-month staging/CI cloud infrastructure spend by using a shared/lower-tier environment for the first month instead of a dedicated staging slot.
reductions.effect: Cuts non-labour infra cost by one month's worth; slightly increases risk of environment contention during early development.
